safetyNote: The Lactifluus volemus group is listed as edible by DGfM and Swiss VAPKO. Eat only confidently identified, sound specimens after adequate cooking. A dry orange-brown cap and abundant white latex that stains gills brown are useful, but several close species share this appearance; European research resolves three species in the traditional L. volemus concept, with intermediate forms requiring molecular data. DGfM flags the broad group as specially protected and on Germany's pre-warning Red List, so check local collecting rules and avoid unnecessary harvesting.

sections.title: Warm russet, dry cap
sections.text: The cap is roughly 5–16 cm across, initially convex with a tucked margin and later nearly flat to slightly depressed. Its dry surface is smooth, finely velvety or faintly wrinkled, sometimes cracking in dry weather. Colour ranges from ochre and cinnamon to apricot-brown, orange-brown or darker brick-red; the edge can be paler. Firm, pale cream flesh may slowly brown on injury. The sturdy stem is usually similar to or a little lighter than the cap.

sections.title: Profuse white milk and browning gills
sections.text: The rather close cream to pale yellow gills are attached to slightly decurrent and sometimes fork near the stem. Scratches quickly release copious white or watery-white latex; the gills and damaged tissue develop reddish-brown to brown marks as it dries. The mild milk is visually very different from the scant or intensely peppery milk of several other lactifluids. A characteristic herring-like or fishy odour can be noticeable, though smell varies with specimen condition. The spore deposit is whitish to pale cream.

sections.title: Woodland and a species group
sections.text: This ectomycorrhizal group occurs in broadleaf and conifer woods, especially during warm summer and autumn months. A European multilocus study separated the old broad L. volemus concept into L. volemus, L. oedematopus and L. subvolemus; cap colour can help with some specimens, but intermediates cannot always be named without DNA. Similar American mushrooms should not automatically be assumed to be the same European species. Field identification here is best treated as the L. volemus group.

sections.title: Edibility and conservation
sections.text: DGfM and VAPKO include the group on their food-mushroom lists. The DGfM entry is L. volemus sensu lato and carries a German special-protection sign and Red List warning category V; these are regional designations, not a universal status. Identify the entire mushroom and its latex reaction before considering food use, and follow local collection limits. The illustration can depict the milk and browning but cannot prove a strict molecular species name.

traits: Dry ochre to apricot or russet-brown cap, about 5–16 cm, smooth to faintly velvety, sometimes cracking
Close cream to pale yellow gills, attached to slightly decurrent, sometimes forked
Copious white latex that dries brownish and stains injured gills reddish-brown
Stout firm stem near cap colour or paler; pale flesh slowly browning
Characteristic herring-like or fishy odour, variable with specimen condition
European L. volemus sensu lato includes several close species, some requiring DNA to resolve
